placement.claim: A repository-local shared claim-evidence capability is the probable canonical owner of the closed production record contract and transport-neutral operations. Domain workflows own their judgments and profiles; a Codex skill and external MCP adapter are projections over the same owner.

reopening_conditions: A real proposal-research or review consumer cannot discover applicable claims without domain semantics that would make the shared core misleading.

The minimum production schema cannot represent exact subjects, evidence baselines, authority, limitations, sensitivity, lineage, reliance, and truthful projection completeness without absorbing domain-owned judgment.
A transport-neutral operation cannot give Codex skills and external read-only MCP consumers equivalent state meaning and provenance.
Authority-bound publication cannot distinguish attribution from admission or prevent an unauthorized producer from exercising a domain transition.
Representative production queries require a canonical database or runtime service rather than a rebuildable projection over durable records.

authority.decision_owner: user or future explicitly authorized portfolio owner

relationships.rationale: This candidate isolates the production substrate and interface from the semantic parent's complete lifecycle so it can be accepted and implemented without claiming the later operational phase is complete.
The later operational phase requires stable production claim identities, exact revisions, authority-bound publication, reliance records, and truthful query projections from this interface.
Revision-bound review findings are an initial domain profile and consumer while retaining ownership of reviewer episodes, severity, synthesis, and review outcomes.
Proposal packets may rely on exact claim revisions while continuing to own proposal identity, meaning, lifecycle, and decision authority.
